questions.question: When you start the vehicle during the pre-trip inspection, the coolant temperature should:
questions.explanation: After starting your vehicle, watch the gauges. The coolant temperature should gradually rise to normal operating temperature.

questions.question: If you lose hydraulic brake pressure, you should do all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: If you lose hydraulic brake pressure, downshift, pump the brakes, and use the parking brake. Find a safe place to stop, such as an escape ramp, open field, or side street.

questions.question: What is the main cause of death and injury in work zones?
questions.explanation: Speeding is the leading cause of death and injury in work zones. Drive carefully when near road workers.

questions.question: When pulled over on the side of the road, a driver should:
questions.explanation: If you stop on the side of the road, turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. This is especially important at night.

questions.question: The overhead inside mirror should be adjusted to see:

options.text: Outside of the driver's side of the bus.
All of the students on the bus.
Students in the first four rows of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the students on the bus.
questions.explanation: Position the overhead inside rearview mirror to show the top of the bus's rear window. This lets you see all students on the bus, including those sitting directly behind you.

questions.question: Broken suspension parts:

options.text: Should be repaired but not right away.

questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up the vehicle and keeps axles in place. Check for damaged or missing spring hangers, spring leaves, shock absorbers, u-bolts, and frame members. Broken suspension parts are very dangerous.

questions.question: If you are in a crash, basic procedures should include all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: If you are in a crash, do three things: protect the area, call the proper authorities, and help anyone injured. Protect the accident site right away to prevent another crash in the same spot.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Cannot be used on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
Help you see a wider area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see a wider area.
questions.explanation: Many large vehicles use curved convex mirrors. Convex mirrors let drivers see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, they make objects look smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: When inspecting a vehicle, you must show each of the following, except:

options.text: The oil pressure gauge is working.
The oil pressure warning light turns off, or the gauge shows normal or increasing pressure.
The oil temperature gauge, if present, rises to normal operating temperature.
The oil pressure gauge comes on when you use the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The oil pressure gauge comes on when you use the brakes.
questions.explanation: When checking the oil pressure gauge during a vehicle inspection, make sure it works. The gauge should show normal or increasing oil pressure, or the warning light should turn off. If there is an oil temperature gauge, it should gradually rise to normal operating temperature.

questions.question: Which of the following is a good rule when making a turn?

options.text: Use your arms to get other drivers' attention.
Turn off your turn signal before turning to avoid confusing other drivers.

questions.explanation: Signal well before you turn so drivers behind you know your plans. Keep your signal on during the turn and turn it off when the turn is complete.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Back up quickly to get out of other drivers' way.
Try not to use your mirrors.

questions.explanation: Backing up a large vehicle is always risky because you cannot see everything behind you. If you must back up, ask someone to help you if you can.

questions.question: If you approach a drawbridge with no signal light or traffic control attendant, you should:

options.text: Speed up to cross the drawbridge quickly.
Wait for another driver to cross first.
Stop, look, and make sure the bridge is fully closed before crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, look, and make sure the bridge is fully closed before crossing.
questions.explanation: Always stop at any drawbridge without a signal light or traffic control attendant. Stop at least 50 feet before the bridge opening and make sure it is completely closed before you cross.

questions.question: Most drivers are least alert:
questions.explanation: Tiredness and loss of attention are major dangers when driving at night. Most people are least alert at night, especially after midnight.

questions.question: The safe maximum amount of play on a 20-inch steering wheel is:
questions.explanation: A steering wheel with more than 10 degrees of play may be broken. On a 20-inch wheel, this equals about two inches of movement at the rim.

questions.question: Before driving, access panels should be:
questions.explanation: Inspect the outside of your bus before driving. Make sure all emergency exits and access panels are closed.

questions.question: When carrying a wide load, you should:

options.text: Get special permits and follow special rules.
Honk at other drivers to make them move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get special permits and follow special rules.
questions.explanation: Loads that are too long, too wide, or too heavy may need special permits. These vehicles usually can only drive at certain times.

questions.question: If your vehicle is hydroplaning, you should:
questions.explanation: If your vehicle starts to hydroplane, do not brake. Instead, release the accelerator and push the clutch in. This will slow your vehicle and help it regain traction.

questions.question: Loading and unloading a school bus:

options.text: Does not need to be supervised.
Can be done while the driver talks to another driver.

questions.explanation: More students are killed while loading or unloading school buses than while riding on them. Drivers must follow safety rules during loading and unloading. This must be done with care and close supervision.

questions.question: Parking brakes:

options.text: Should be tested only after driving a distance.
Should be tested on a hill.

questions.explanation: Always check parking brakes before driving as part of your pre-trip inspection. If the parking brakes do not hold, the vehicle is unsafe and must be fixed.

questions.question: If the brakes pull to one side when you use them, it means:

options.text: The brakes need to be checked.
The brakes have too much stopping power.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes need to be checked.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle pulls to one side when braking, you may have a brake problem. Fix the problem before driving. Driving an unsafe vehicle breaks federal and state laws.
